I'le read it to you, Mr. Aymwell ; I receiued your let ter, and praise your apprehension, vpon the first view of your person, I conceiu'd opinion of your merit, the flame is now too great to bee supprest, it is no time to protract your hopes nor dishonour in mee to yeild vpon noble conditions at the first summon, I accept your loue, and re quire your industry to preuent my fathers purpose, my ser uant Sensible you may trust, I will vse some inuention to de lay my expected marriage, farewell. De'e know this charracter, where's my man Braines. Oh my best seruant. Does not thy very soule blush to deceiue me. Where's Sensible Enter Sensible. For your good seruice to your Mistris housewife Packe vp your trinckets, I here discharge you. I loue you but too well, goe to your chamber. I like it well. It shall be my next worke: Who shall with her? Braines. Letters! Your patience Sir. A Conspiracy. My man Braines is arrested by your Tutor, a plot to take away my daughter, she is gone. I'me rent with vexation, Sirra goe you with me to the Prison. Exit George and Messenger. Thou? I haue lost my daughter. Not, not, and yet this old Ruffian will not let me vex for it, he sayes the greatest losse is his. Your happinesse removes my affliction, ha! Forbeare, where is my daughter? villaine confesse. Sir Nicholas : Here's my daughter. Marryed to Aymwell ! You have wonne it Be my lov'd children, and I wish a ioy Flow in all Bosomes. Braines we are reconcil'd.
speeches.Bra:: What's the matter Mistris. Good Sir. And write too the superscription of a Letter or so. I hope you are Sensible. Let me councell you not to expresse any violence in your passions, least you marre the possibility of reclay ming her, it seemes Aymwell ha's mist the intelligence, where shame is inforc'd too much vpon the delinquent, it begets rather an audacious defence of the sin, then repen tance, soft raine slides to the root, and nourishes, where great stormes make a noyse, wet but the skin a'th earth, and runne away in a channell. Bu'y sweet Mistris Sensible, I hope wee shall meete againe as merry as we part. By all meanes let it be suddaine. I wo'not sleepe, till shee be married, but carry things smooth, let not the Knight suspect y'are troubled, your daughter will be fetc'ht about with a byas againe. Hereafter for my sake, and subtle paines Who ere is wise, let the world call him Braines. Sir. point me a minute to returne with her, if I faile put my braines into'th pot, and let 'em be seru'd vp with a Calues head, to morrow dinner. Come Mistris will you walke, I would faine see any mortall wit couzen me a my charge now, I will liue to be the shame of Pollititians, and when I am dead, be clapt vp into the Chronicles. I.
speeches.Geo:: I'th height and puzze of my care to make Thee, happie? to conspire thy ouerthrow I wo'not heare. Which of my cares reward'st thou with this folly. Dispute it not. Take 'em all we'e and be gone. So, things must be mannag'd wisely, I will hasten the marriage. Within two dayes — to morrow. How thou deseru'st me, let vs in. How Sir? Waite on my daughter to the Exchange, obserue her carefully.
speeches.Man:: Come ha you finisht your discourse yet.
speeches.Both:: You know you may commaund vs.
speeches.Clar:: I refuse no office To aduance your hopes.
speeches.Nic:: By this gold she shall Father, lay it out in Tooth picks, I'le weare 'em out in my hat; come I'le with you for the lycence.
We arrest you Sir. We charge you i'th Kings name obey vs,
speeches.Tut,: Away with him to Prison, 'tis no slight action, at your perils Sergeants—my fayrest Mistris.
Your servant Braines remembers his duty in this Paper.
Well met friend, what? thou lookest sad. What's the Newes? Mr. Iohn Fowler. It cannot be, I saw him but this morning Lusty and pleasant, how dyed hee? Where? Dead! He was a Sutor to Master Worthies daughter. How poore a thing is life, that we cannot Promise a Minutes certainty, i'th height And strength of youth, falling to dust agen. He was a noble Fellow, and deserves A memory, if my braine have not lost All his Poeticke juyce, it shall goe hard But Ile squeeze out an Elegie. Sir I heard ill newes, Master Fowlers dead. Where's his body? It is a duty which without invitement We are both prompt to discharge. Assured your ends are noble, we are happy in'. I doubt the proiect.
You will excuse me, and beare a part, when I tell the cause. Our Friend Master Fowler 's dead. The same. Suddenly. At Master Worthies house. Too true Sir. Mistris Penelope, right. 'Tis the last Office I can doe him, now to waite on him to the Earth. Cry mercy Sir, pray keepe your way. We must hope the best, he was an inconstant young man ▪ frequenting of some companies, had corrupted his nature, and a little debauched him.
speeches.VVhib:: Where is Sir Nicholas ? we have brought the Gentleman.
Yes Sir Nicholas, hath Mistris Violetta, I am a witnesse.
speeches.Tut:: I pray y' sir let it be forgotten, I ha bin kickt for't.
We are Witnesses. We are witnesses of that too.
Franck thou art married, and Sir Nicholas has made a Lady, I ha liv'd loose a great while, and doe purpose to be made fast to this Gentlewoman. To whose act I owe my true Conversion. When all things have their tryall, you shall find. Nothing is constant but a vertuous mind. Exeunt.
